subjective.citation_text: Patient: I'm 45 years old, male. I came in because I've been having pain in my right elbow for about a week. It started when I was playing lacrosse with my kids, and it hurts whenever I move it. Doctor: Could you please confirm your age, gender, and describe the nature of the pain in your right elbow, including any specific activities that aggravate or relieve it? Patient: I'm 45, male. The pain is sharp and happens anytime I move my elbow. It started when I was playing lacrosse with my kids, and my son hit me with the stick. It radiates down my forearm, and it's been hurting me ever since. Doctor: Have you noticed any swelling, bruising, or restricted range of motion in your right elbow? Patient: Yes, there's some swelling and a little bruising around the tip of my elbow, and it's pretty painful when I try to move it. Doctor: Have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your hand or fingers since the injury? Patient: No, I haven't had any numbness, tingling, or weakness in my hand or fingers since the injury. The pain is mainly in my elbow and forearm, and I can still move my hand and fingers, though it's uncomfortable. Doctor: Have you experienced any previous elbow injuries or conditions, such as fractures, dislocations, or ligament tears? Patient: No, I don't think I've had any previous elbow injuries or conditions like fractures, dislocations, or ligament tears. This is the first time I've had pain like this in my elbow. Doctor: Can you specify the exact location of the pain in your elbow (e.g., on the outside, inside, or back of the elbow)? Patient: The pain is right at the tip of my elbow, on the back side, and it radiates down my forearm. It's really sharp whenever I move it.
